heading: SIF Minimum Investment Rule: How the ₹10 Lakh Threshold is Calculated
tldr: Specified Investment Funds (SIFs) require a minimum investment of ₹10 lakhs per investor.
This ₹10 lakh threshold is calculated at the investor's Permanent Account Number (PAN) level.
The investment can be spread across various SIF strategies offered by the same Asset Management Company (AMC).
Systematic Investment Plans (SIPs), Systematic Withdrawal Plans (SWPs), and Systematic Transfer Plans (STPs) contribute to or reduce this threshold.
Breaching the minimum by withdrawing below ₹10 lakhs can lead to the fund house liquidating the remaining units.
caption:
Thinking about investing in certain funds? There's a special rule you should know. For some funds (called SIFs), you need to keep at least ₹10 lakhs invested. This total is checked using your PAN number, even if you spread your money across different plans from the same company. If your investment drops below this, your fund house might sell off your remaining units. Learn more about this important rule in our latest article.
